title: Privilege matrix: inline permission editing + member impact simulator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and interaction patterns for a ‘privilege matrix’ editor: a dense, keyboard-accessible grid where org admins can edit role permissions inline, preview effective member access, and see an audit preview before committing changes. This ticket focuses on the UX flows, error guardrails, and microcopy for bulk edits, SSO/SAML role mappings, and a lightweight simulation mode that estimates member impact without changing live assignments. Goal: reduce time-to-edit for complex roles and reduce accidental over-provisioning while preserving auditability and compatibility with RBAC v2 backend APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix UI supports inline toggles for permission primitives (read, write, exec) and dropdowns for conditional scopes
Keyboard-first interactions: tab to cell, space toggles checkbox, enter opens scope editor
Simulator mode shows list of members affected with reason (direct role, inherited, group mapping) and highlights high-risk changes
Bulk apply flow with undo buffer and preview diff before commit
Audit preview section shows a redact-safe summary and links to change request (for enterprises with approval workflow)
Designs include mobile-responsive fallback (compact list) and accessible color contrasts
Edge cases: conflicting SSO mapping rules surfaced with explicit resolution suggestions
tasks: Finalize wireframes for desktop matrix and compact mobile list
Write microcopy for permission states and simulator warnings
Prototype keyboard navigation and announce behavior for screen readers
Coordinate with ENG to define API contract for simulator (estimated affected members) and diff payload
Run 3 usability sessions with platform and tenant-admin personas
engineering_notes: Must integrate with ENG-18855 (simulator backend) and ENG-18902 (bulk apply + audit write API)
Frontend should debounce permission changes and use optimistic preview; final commit must call transaction API that returns per-member change tokens
Consider rendering large orgs with virtualized rows and on-demand member sampling rather than full list
review_feedback: PM (Lena Ortiz): prioritize simulator accuracy over full member listing for initial rollout; sampling + thresholds OK
Security (Arjun Rao): require explicit confirmation for changes that increase admin-level privileges and require 2FA for commit in tenant settings
Eng (Sofia Kim): prefer dropdown for conditional scopes instead of freeform to keep validation simple
decisions: Initial MVP will surface up to 200 affected members in simulator and provide a sampled count for larger orgs
Map SSO group-to-role warnings inline and provide suggested resolution actions (create new mapping or confirm override)
Audit preview will be redact-safe: show permission names and counts, no member PII by default; link expands for full view in private deployments
